newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times front page - Jan 10.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times front page - Jan 10.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following stories on its front page on Friday:

- Bringing to an end a four-year feud between two of the world's largest companies, Volkswagen AG agreed to pay $100 million to the General Motors Corp to settle a lawsuit contending that VW stole trade secrets from GM.

- A tape recording was made of a conference call in which Speaker Newt Gingrich may have violated an agreement he made not to use his office or his allies to organise a counter attack against an ethics committee's charges.

- Under a barage of complaints from Democrats over the timetable for proceeding with the ethics case against Speaker Newt Gingrich, the Republican chairman of the House ethics committee postponed scheduled public hearings next week and ordered the panel's special counsel to complete his report first.
- Two pipe bombs placed in trash bins in a run-down section of Tel Aviv exploded 10 minutes apart, wounding 13 people.
- A twin-engine turboprop plane operated by Comair, an affiliate of Delta Air Lines, crashed in a snowstorm while approaching the Detroit Metropolitan Airport, apparently killing all 26 passengers.
- Arkansas carried out the death penalty against three killers in a single night.
